name: New Orleans Loop — January
subtitle: Luray Caverns · Bristol · Nashville · Memphis · the Delta · Vicksburg · New Orleans · Mobile · Atlanta
summary: Fourteen days from Fort Lee to New Orleans and back, down the inland side of the Appalachians and home along the Gulf and the Piedmont. It is a loop, so no road is driven twice. Carnival opens on 6 January and Mardi Gras is not until 9 February 2027, which puts the far end of this trip inside the season but nowhere near the crush — and in the cheapest, quietest fortnight New Orleans has. 2,926 miles, and not one day over 350.

mustSee.name: Luray Caverns
mustSee.why: A steady 12°C underground on the coldest morning of the trip.

mustSee.name: The Ryman
mustSee.why: For part of every winter the Opry moves back into the Mother Church.

mustSee.name: Country Music Hall of Fame
mustSee.why: The Rotunda at the end of it is worth the ticket on its own.

mustSee.name: Graceland
mustSee.why: The biggest ticket on the route, and nobody regrets it.

mustSee.name: National Civil Rights Museum
mustSee.why: The Lorraine Motel, balcony and all. The thing the older children remember.

mustSee.name: Clarksdale
mustSee.why: The Delta, the Crossroads, and lunch where the blues came from.

mustSee.name: Vicksburg National Military Park
mustSee.why: Sixteen miles of tour road and 1,325 monuments, covered by a $20 vehicle fee.

mustSee.name: Jackson Square
mustSee.why: The cathedral, the Cabildo and the Presbytère on three sides of it.

mustSee.name: Café du Monde
mustSee.why: Beignets since 1862. You will wear the sugar.

mustSee.name: The St Charles streetcar
mustSee.why: 1923 cars, under the live oaks, $1.25 a ride.

mustSee.name: Oak Alley
mustSee.why: Three-hundred-year-old oaks in a quarter-mile tunnel.

mustSee.name: USS Alabama
mustSee.why: Climb down through a battleship for $18 an adult and $6 a child.

watchOuts.title: Every high road in the mountains is shut
watchOuts.text: Skyline Drive closes along its whole 105 miles for days at a time — the entire road was gated ahead of one storm in late January 2026. Most of the Blue Ridge Parkway’s 469 miles sat closed through that month too. Kuwohi Road in the Smokies is gated from 1 December to 31 March every single year. This route is built so that none of it matters: it runs the valley floor on I-81 and spends its mountain morning inside a cave. Do not add a ridge road to the plan and expect it to be open.

watchOuts.title: Four freezing nights, and three more that are a coin toss
watchOuts.text: On the January average, Luray drops to −3°C, Bristol to −2°C, Nashville to 0°C and Fredericksburg to −1°C. Memphis, Atlanta and Charlotte each fall below freezing on roughly two nights in five. Pack for a winter trip at both ends and a mild one in the middle — New Orleans averages 16°C by day and freezes about one night in sixteen.

watchOuts.title: Check the Carnival calendar before you fix the dates
watchOuts.text: Carnival 2027 opens on Twelfth Night, Wednesday 6 January, with four parades that evening — the Phunny Phorty Phellows on a streetcar, the Funky Uptown Krewe behind them, the Société des Champs Élysée, and the Joan of Arc walking parade through the Quarter at eight. Mardi Gras itself is 9 February 2027, four weeks after this trip ends. Landing in New Orleans on or just after the 6th gets you the season’s opening at January prices; landing in February gets you a different holiday and a much bigger bill.

watchOuts.title: The alligators are asleep
watchOuts.text: Louisiana alligators brumate from about November to late February. A January swamp tour out of Barataria or Pearl River is a beautiful boat ride through bald cypress with almost no reptiles in it. Sell it to the children that way, or spend the afternoon at Oak Alley instead. This is the one place where a Florida winter genuinely beats a Louisiana one.

watchOuts.title: Nobody grits the Natchez Trace
watchOuts.text: The Parkway is never plowed, salted or sanded, and because it is lined with trees it holds ice long after the roads beside it have cleared. It closed south of Nashville for black ice and fallen trees in January 2025. This route only uses the twenty miles at the Natchez end, and US-61 runs parallel the whole way as a fallback — take it if there has been any freezing rain.

watchOuts.title: Two time zone crossings, and the second one hurts
watchOuts.text: You gain an hour near Crossville on day 3 and give it straight back between Montgomery and Atlanta on day 11. Day 11 is already the second-longest drive of the fortnight at 328 miles; on the clock it costs seven hours, not six. Start it early.

watchOuts.title: Sunday closes the Delta
watchOuts.text: Count the days forward before you book. The Delta Blues Museum shuts on Sundays and a good deal of Clarksdale goes with it, which would gut day 6. Moving the departure by a single day fixes it, and it is much cheaper to notice now than on US-61.

watchOuts.title: The last four days are the price of the loop
watchOuts.text: Days 11 to 14 cover 1,202 miles with Montgomery, Atlanta and Charlotte the only things on them. This is what a loop costs: the alternative is driving back up the Mississippi the way you came. It is still gentler than an out-and-back — no day on this route passes 350 miles, where a Florida run has two over 400.

watchOuts.title: Graceland and the aquarium are where the ticket money goes
watchOuts.text: Six people at Graceland is around $430 and the Georgia Aquarium is $350 to $425. Between them they are most of the entry-fee budget. Everything else on this route is $20 a vehicle, $18 a head or free — Vicksburg, the Trace, Emerald Mound, the Fredericksburg battlefield, the Peabody ducks and the Parthenon grounds cost almost nothing.

watchOuts.title: Six people, one vehicle, thirteen nights
watchOuts.text: A seven-seat minivan seats everyone but the space behind the third row will not take a fortnight of luggage for six. Either budget for a roof box or take a full-size SUV, which costs more to hire and roughly $130 more in fuel over this distance. Price both before you book, and book the vehicle by seatbelt count rather than by what the listing photograph suggests.

pros: A genuine loop. 2,926 miles and not one of them driven twice — down the inland side of the Appalachians, home along the Gulf and the Piedmont.
Carnival opens on 6 January 2027 and Mardi Gras is not until 9 February, so New Orleans is inside the season and still in the cheapest, quietest fortnight of its year.
No day over 350 miles, and three of the fourteen have no drive in them at all.
Three nights in New Orleans, which is the longest single stop on any route on this site.
Nashville and Memphis on the same line: the Ryman, the Hall of Fame, Graceland, Sun Studio and the Lorraine Motel inside three days.
Almost no tolls between Virginia and Louisiana. The entire middle of this trip is free road.
The far end is mild. New Orleans averages 16°C by day in January and freezes about one night in sixteen.
cons: Four nights below freezing and three more that could go either way. This is a winter trip for the first three days and the last two.
The mountains are scenery seen from the valley floor. Every high road on the route is gated for the season.
Days 11 to 14 are 1,202 miles of interstate with three cities on them and not much else.
Only New Orleans and Memphis get more than one night. Nashville gets an evening and a morning, which is not enough.
The alligators are dormant, so a swamp tour is a boat ride through cypress rather than a wildlife trip.
2,926 miles is nearly twice the Southwest Loop, and three children in the back will know it.

notConsidered.place: The Blue Ridge Parkway and Skyline Drive
notConsidered.reason: January shuts them. Most of the Parkway's 469 miles sat closed through January 2026, and Skyline Drive closes along its entire 105 miles for days at a time — the whole road was gated ahead of a single storm in late January 2026. This route runs the valley floor on I-81 instead and spends its mountain morning inside Luray Caverns, which is 12°C in any weather.

Kuwohi Road, the old Clingmans Dome Road, is gated from 1 December to 31 March every year without exception, Newfound Gap Road closes intermittently in snow, and Dollywood is shut for the winter. The park is 130 miles off the line for a version of itself with the best bits locked.

9 February 2027, four weeks after this trip ends. Carnival 2027 is one of the shortest on record at 34 days, and the fortnight before Fat Tuesday is when New Orleans lodging triples and the Quarter becomes impassable. Going in January buys the season's opening at a fifth of the price.

notConsidered.place: The Natchez Trace Parkway, end to end
notConsidered.reason: 444 miles at 50 mph is two full days, it is never plowed, salted or sanded, and it holds ice long after the roads beside it have cleared. It also runs Nashville to Natchez by way of Tupelo, which means giving up Memphis and the Delta. This route drives the best twenty miles of it, at the Natchez end, and takes US-61 for the rest.
The Key West Run already owns I-95, the Atlantic coast and the whole of Florida. Repeating any of it would make this the same holiday twice.

Rock City and the Incline Railway would suit the children, but Chattanooga sits 120 miles north of the Mobile-to-Atlanta line and there is no day spare to reach it. It belongs on a trip that comes home through Tennessee.

notConsidered.place: A fourth night in New Orleans
notConsidered.reason: It would have to come out of Memphis, and Memphis at one night means choosing between Graceland and the Lorraine Motel. Three nights at the far point and a full day in Memphis is the better trade.
The Alamo is another 550 miles west of New Orleans, which is a third of the way to Los Angeles. It would turn a loop into a crossing and add four days.

moneySavers.item: Do not buy the national park pass
moneySavers.detail: This is the rare route where it does not pay. The only fee stations on it are Harpers Ferry and Vicksburg, at $20 a vehicle each. The Natchez Trace, Emerald Mound, Barataria and the Fredericksburg battlefield are all free. Buy the pass only if you already know you will use it again before it expires.

moneySavers.item: Sleep in Metairie or Mid-City, not the Quarter
moneySavers.detail: January is the cheapest stretch of the New Orleans year and the Quarter still charges a premium for the postcode. Mid-City puts you on the Canal streetcar; Metairie is fifteen minutes out and half the price, with parking that is free rather than $45 a night.

moneySavers.item: Hire from a neighbourhood branch, not Newark Airport
moneySavers.detail: You are not flying, so there is no reason to pay the airport concession fee. A seven-seat van out of Jersey City runs around $60 to $75 a day in January against far more at Newark.

The Elvis Experience at about $85 covers the mansion, the car museum and both aircraft. The VIP and Ultimate tiers add front-of-queue and a keepsake book, which for a party of six is several hundred dollars for a shorter wait in the quietest month of the year.

moneySavers.item: The Center for Civil and Human Rights instead of the Georgia Aquarium
moneySavers.detail: Around $120 for six against $350 or more, and for children over about ten it is the better morning. If the aquarium is non-negotiable, book online for a weekday — the gate price is $70.77.

moneySavers.item: A $3 Jazzy Pass, not four single fares
moneySavers.detail: Unlimited streetcars, buses and the Algiers ferry for a day. Six single streetcar rides cost $7.50 before you have gone anywhere twice.

moneySavers.item: Eat lunch in the Delta and dinner in the cities
moneySavers.detail: Clarksdale, Vicksburg and Natchez do a proper hot lunch for a third of what the same food costs in Nashville or the French Quarter. Load the middle of the day where the route is cheap.
$36 an adult and $18 for 6 to 12, and the online price beats the window. Six people through the gate is $162 either way you cut it, so take the discount.

options.name: Car and lodging
options.tagline: A hired van, thirteen nights booked, and every stop reachable
options.summary: The straightforward build and the one this route is designed around. Hire a seven-seat van at home, book thirteen nights, and keep the vehicle small enough to park in the French Quarter, downtown Nashville and downtown Memphis. Costs more per night than camping and around $800 less to fuel over this distance.

vehicle.detail: Chrysler Pacifica · Honda Odyssey · Toyota Sienna · Chevrolet Suburban
vehicle.notes: Nothing on this route needs four-wheel drive. What it needs is a scraper in the boot and tyres with tread on them, because days 1 to 3 and day 13 run through country that ices overnight. Hire from a neighbourhood branch rather than Newark Airport — you are not flying, so there is no reason to pay the concession fee.

costs.notes: Best value sleeps out of the centre everywhere — Metairie rather than the Quarter, Southaven rather than downtown Memphis — and skips the two dearest tickets. Best location is walkable in every city and takes everything. The gap is almost entirely lodging, parking and two entry fees.

pros: Parks anywhere. The French Quarter, downtown Nashville and downtown Memphis are all walk-from-the-car stops.
Roughly $800 less in fuel than the motorhome over 3,000 miles.
No plumbing to freeze on days 1, 2, 3, 13 and 14, which is when this route is actually cold.
Three of the fourteen days have no drive at all, so the vehicle sits still for a quarter of the trip.
cons: Lodging is the largest line in the budget by a distance.
The four days home are spent belted into seats.

5.label: Two car parks:
5.text: Graceland’s own is about $10 and the shuttle across the boulevard is included. Downtown Memphis hotel parking is $25 to $35 a night on top of that.

8.label: Park once for three days:
8.text: The Quarter is thirteen blocks by six and walkable end to end. The streetcar covers everything outside it for $3 a day.

12.label: Book ahead:
12.text: The Georgia Aquarium is $70.77 at the gate and around $55 booked online for a weekday. For six that is a $95 difference for two minutes of admin.

options.name: Motorhome
options.tagline: Cheaper at the bottom, colder at both ends, and no use in New Orleans
options.summary: A Class C hired in New Jersey. On paper it lands within $500 of the car build at the low end — the campground and food savings very nearly cover the hire and the fuel. What decides it is not money. It is a winterized rig leaving a freezing New Jersey, private campgrounds shut for the season on the two coldest nights, and a 30-footer that cannot go into the French Quarter, downtown Nashville or downtown Memphis — which is most of what this route is for.

vehicle.detail: Sleeps 6 to 7 · 6 to 7 seatbelts · roughly 8 mpg
vehicle.notes: Book by seatbelt count rather than sleeping capacity, and get the mileage allowance in writing: at 2,926 miles a 100-mile daily cap adds around $500. Ask specifically whether the unit is winterized, what de-winterizing costs, and who pays if a pipe splits in the Shenandoah.

lines.basis: Class C hired in New Jersey. Peer-to-peer listings run $175 to $225 a night in winter.
Peer-to-peer hires typically include 100 to 150 miles a day. This route averages 209.
New Jersey rigs are drained from mid-October to late March
About 3,050 miles at 8 mpg, at $3.30 a gallon. This is the line that decides the argument.

Cooking in the motorhome with a few meals out

costs.notes: The low column assumes a flat-rate hire with unlimited mileage and state park sites wherever they can be had. The high column is a peer-to-peer hire with a daily mileage cap and private parks at winter rates. The spread is wider than the car build because more of it is outside your control.

pros: The four days home are far more bearable when three children can get out of their seats.
No check-ins, and the food line drops by around $650.
Gulf-side state parks in January are genuinely cheap, and the Trace has free campgrounds.
Graceland has its own RV park, which is the one stop where it wins outright.
cons: About $800 more in fuel at 8 mpg over 3,000 miles.
Winterized at both ends of the trip, with any freeze damage charged to you.
The two coldest nights are the two where private campgrounds are most likely to be closed for the season.
Barred or awkward at New Orleans, Nashville and Memphis — three of the four reasons to come.

1.label: Winterized:
1.text: New Jersey rigs are drained from mid-October to late March. De-winterize one and you leave a freezing New Jersey with live plumbing, and a split pipe is charged to you.

2.label: Most sites are shut:
2.text: Private campgrounds in the Shenandoah and around the Tri-Cities close for the winter. What stays open is state park sites with no hook-ups, on the two coldest nights of the fortnight.

5.label: The day it wins outright:
5.text: Graceland has its own RV park across Elvis Presley Boulevard. You park, and you walk to the gates.

7.label: Scout Emerald Mound first:
7.text: Vicksburg’s tour road takes a motorhome without trouble. The Emerald Mound car park is small and reached by a minor road — look at it on the map before you commit a 30-footer to it.

8.label: Not into the Quarter:
8.text: Nothing that size goes into the French Quarter. The RV parks are out on the industrial canal or across the river, and you come in by bus, streetcar or ferry — which works, but it is not what you hired it for.

10.label: Made for this day:
10.text: US-90 along the Mississippi coast is flat and straight, and the Gulf-side state parks are the cheapest nights on the route.

13.label: Freezing again:
13.text: Northern Virginia in January, and most campgrounds within reach of Fredericksburg are closed for the season. This is the night the motorhome costs you a hotel anyway.

days.headline: Off the Turnpike and into the Shenandoah
days.notes: Fort Lee is on the west bank of the Hudson, which is the one gift the start of this trip gives you: no bridge toll, no Manhattan. Then turn inland rather than south — I-78 across New Jersey and Pennsylvania, down the Great Valley on I-81, and east on US-211 over the Blue Ridge into Luray. Very little of it is scenic and the last forty minutes are, climbing through Thornton Gap with the ridge on both sides. If you are running ahead, Harpers Ferry sits almost on the line: a town wedged into the point where the Shenandoah meets the Potomac, with two states looking back at you across the water.
activities: Out by 7am — I-78 is unforgiving after eight
Harpers Ferry if you are ahead of the clock
Book the 9am Luray Caverns tour before you go to bed

days.headline: The mountain day, spent underground
days.notes: Skyline Drive starts half an hour from here and in January it is very often shut — all 105 miles of it, sometimes for days at a time. That is fine, because nothing on this route needs it. Luray Caverns opens at nine, sits at a constant 12°C whatever is happening above it, and the tour is a mile and a quarter of paved, well-lit path past columns the height of a house. Out by eleven and the rest is I-81 down the valley, with the Blue Ridge on your left the whole afternoon. Bristol at the end of it is one town in two states, and the line runs down the middle of State Street with a brass marker set into the tarmac.
activities: Luray Caverns at 9am — the first tour is the empty one
The Great Stalacpipe Organ, played on the formations themselves
Natural Bridge is fifteen minutes off I-81 at exit 180

days.headline: Into Central Time, and into the Ryman
days.notes: The Birthplace of Country Music Museum opens at ten and takes about ninety minutes. It is built around the 1927 Bristol Sessions — the fortnight of recordings in a hat warehouse on State Street that put the Carter Family and Jimmie Rodgers onto disc and started the entire industry. Then I-81 into I-40 past Knoxville, and somewhere near Crossville you cross into Central Time and get an hour back. Spend it in Nashville: for a stretch of every winter the Grand Ole Opry leaves its purpose-built house out by the airport and moves back downtown into the Ryman, which is the version worth seeing.
activities: Birthplace of Country Music Museum from 10am
You gain an hour at the time zone line near Crossville
Check the Opry's Ryman dates before you fix your departure — in 2026 it was 2 to 10 January

pois.name: The Ryman Auditorium
pois.caption: A tabernacle built in 1892, the Opry’s home for thirty years, and its home again for a stretch of every winter.

photos.caption: A tabernacle built in 1892, the Opry’s home for thirty years, and its home again for a stretch of every winter.

days.headline: A morning on Music Row, then west
days.notes: The shortest driving day of the fortnight, which makes the morning a real one. The Country Music Hall of Fame is the pick — two or three hours, ending in the Rotunda, a circular room of bronze plaques under 'Will the Circle Be Unbroken' cut into the stone. If the children have had their fill of country music, the Parthenon in Centennial Park is a full-scale concrete replica of the one in Athens with a 42-foot gilded Athena standing inside it, and the park around it costs nothing. Away by one and I-40 has you in Memphis in daylight.

The Parthenon in Centennial Park — free to walk around outside
Leave by 1pm to reach Memphis before dark

days.headline: Graceland, the Lorraine Motel, and one small room on Union Avenue
days.notes: The heaviest day on the route and the best. Graceland opens at nine and the Elvis Experience — the house, the cars, the two jets — takes most of a morning; it is nine miles south of downtown and the biggest single ticket on this trip at about $85 an adult. Come back into town for the National Civil Rights Museum, which is built into and around the Lorraine Motel with the balcony left exactly as it was on 4 April 1968. Three hours, $18 an adult and $15 for 5 to 17, and it will be the thing the older children still talk about in a year. Sun Studio sits between the two: half an hour in one small room where Elvis, Cash, Perkins and Lewis all recorded. If anything is left in the tank, the Peabody ducks come down to the lobby fountain at eleven and go back up at five, and cost nothing at all.

days.headline: Down Highway 61
days.notes: US-61 leaves Memphis and drops onto the flattest ground you will ever drive across. This is the Delta: cotton stubble to the horizon in January, catfish ponds, grain elevators, and small towns that handed the blues to everyone who came afterwards. Clarksdale is the stop. The Delta Blues Museum is in the old freight depot, is open ten to five Monday to Saturday and closed on Sundays, and is small enough to do properly in an hour. The junction of 61 and 49 is signposted as the Crossroads, and Ground Zero Blues Club a few streets away does lunch. Then south through Cleveland and Leland, over the Yazoo, and up onto the bluff at Vicksburg — the first high ground since Memphis.

days.headline: A siege, a mound, and a city after dark
days.notes: Vicksburg National Military Park has a 16-mile tour road that opens at 8:30 and runs past 1,325 monuments and markers strung along the ridges either side of it — two hours at a stop-and-look pace. The USS Cairo sits in the middle of it: an ironclad gunboat mined on the Yazoo in December 1862, salvaged a century later, and open to the sky under a canopy so you can see straight down into her timbers. Then US-61 south. Twenty minutes short of Natchez, Emerald Mound is a free, unstaffed eight-acre platform mound you can simply walk up, and a mile beyond it the Natchez Trace Parkway ends after 444 miles. Natchez itself deserves an hour on the bluff. New Orleans is three hours further and you will arrive in the dark, which is the right way to arrive.

days.headline: The Quarter on foot
days.notes: The French Quarter is thirteen blocks by six and walking is the only sensible way through it. Jackson Square first, with St Louis Cathedral behind it and the Cabildo and the Presbytère on either side — both are state museums and both are cheap. Café du Monde is on the corner and has done beignets and chicory café au lait since 1862; it is no longer the round-the-clock place it used to be, opening at 7:15am and closing at eleven most nights, and you will wear the sugar whatever you do. The French Market runs down Decatur behind it. Then the National WWII Museum over in the Warehouse District, which is enormous and genuinely takes half a day. If Carnival has opened, the evening belongs to whatever is rolling.
activities: Jackson Square and St Louis Cathedral first thing
Café du Monde — go before nine in the morning or late at night
The National WWII Museum, half a day, about $32 an adult
Royal Street for the buskers; Bourbon Street for about ten minutes

days.driveTime: 1h 40m round trip if you go to Oak Alley
days.headline: Streetcars, oaks and the river road
days.notes: Day two gets you out of the Quarter. The St Charles line is the oldest continuously operating streetcar in the world, running 1923 Perley Thomas cars up under the live oaks past the Garden District to Audubon Park — $1.25 a ride, or $3 for a one-day Jazzy Pass that also covers the buses and the ferry. Get off around Washington Avenue and walk the Garden District, which is a grid of galleried mansions and cast-iron fences and takes about an hour. In the afternoon either drive an hour up the River Road to Oak Alley, whose quarter-mile tunnel of 300-year-old live oaks is one of the genuine sights of the South, or take a swamp boat out of Barataria. Be warned about the swamp: in January the alligators are dormant.
activities: A $3 Jazzy Pass beats paying four single fares
Walk the Garden District from Washington Avenue
Oak Alley — $30 adult, $9 for 6 to 17, an hour each way
City Park and the Louisiana Children's Museum if it rains

days.headline: The easy day, and a battleship
days.notes: Deliberately the lightest day of the fortnight, because three long ones come after it. Out of New Orleans across the Rigolets and then US-90 along the Mississippi coast rather than I-10 — twenty-odd miles of white sand on your right, the Biloxi Lighthouse standing on the central reservation of the highway, and Ocean Springs with its shrimp fleet tied up at the end of it. Mobile by mid-afternoon, which leaves the whole of the USS Alabama. You climb down through a 35,000-ton battleship and through the submarine moored alongside her for $18 an adult and $6 a child, and it is comfortably the best-value ticket on this route.
activities: US-90 along the coast, not I-10
The Biloxi Lighthouse really is in the middle of the road
USS Alabama and USS Drum — last entry around 4pm

days.headline: North on I-65, and the hour comes back
days.notes: The longest day since the drive down, and the clock makes it worse: somewhere between Montgomery and Atlanta you cross into Eastern Time and give back the hour you picked up in Tennessee. Montgomery is almost exactly halfway and costs you nothing in distance. The Rosa Parks Museum stands on the corner where she was arrested in December 1955, and Dexter Avenue Baptist Church, where a 26-year-old King was pastor, is four blocks up the hill in the shadow of the state capitol. An hour there breaks the day in the right place. Then I-85 into Atlanta.
activities: Break at Montgomery — the Rosa Parks Museum takes about an hour
Dexter Avenue Baptist Church, four blocks below the capitol
You lose an hour crossing into Eastern Time
Atlanta by early evening

days.headline: A morning in Atlanta, then the Piedmont
days.notes: A short drive, so the morning is yours. The Georgia Aquarium is the obvious call and the expensive one — $55 to $70 a head depending on the date, so $350 and up for six. The Center for Civil and Human Rights next door is about a third of that and pitched better at children over ten, and the World of Coca-Cola is on the same plaza. Then I-85 north-east through the Piedmont, which is 240 miles of pine, red clay and outlet malls, with Charlotte at the end of it.
activities: Georgia Aquarium, booked ahead, or the Center for Civil and Human Rights
The BeltLine Eastside Trail if the sun is out
Discovery Place Science in Charlotte if you land early

days.headline: The long one, and the cold comes back
days.notes: The hardest day of the return and the only one over 340 miles. I-85 to Petersburg and then I-95 north — the first time this trip has touched I-95 since the morning it left home. Fredericksburg is chosen over Richmond deliberately: it is 55 miles further up the road, which takes an hour off tomorrow, and the old town is four walkable blocks of eighteenth-century brick running down to the Rappahannock. The battlefield and the Sunken Road are on the edge of town and free. It will also be the first properly cold night since Nashville.
activities: Leave early — this is the day with no slack in it
Fredericksburg battlefield and the Sunken Road, free
Caroline Street for dinner

days.headline: Home the short way
days.notes: Under six hours, and the only real variable is what time you meet Washington and Baltimore. Leave before seven and you are through both before the day properly starts; leave at nine and you will add an hour to the drive and a good deal more to everyone's temper. I-95 the whole way, over the Delaware Memorial Bridge, up the Turnpike, and into Fort Lee from the south with no bridge to cross at the end of it.
activities: Out before 7am to clear the Beltway and the Harbor Tunnel
Last fuel in Delaware or New Jersey
Home by mid-afternoon
